s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological syndrome with rapid progression of motor and autonomic dysfunction
key_facts: 42-year-old man with 30 pack-years of smoking
Cannabis use, alcohol dependence, and use of herbal products
3-day history of acute symptoms
Marked paraparesis of the lower limbs (muscle strength 2/5)
Normal sensory function, including proprioception, light touch, and vibration
Normal cranial nerve and upper limb examinations
Febrile and respiratory distress requiring intubation and sedation
Clear cerebrospinal fluid without albuminocytologic dissociation
Abnormal blood tests, including anemia, leukocytosis, and elevated liver enzymes
Multiple bilateral, symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions on brain MRI
Diffuse T2 hyperintensities throughout the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar cord on spinal MRI

shortlist.label: Acute Transverse Myelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of motor and autonomic dysfunction with spinal cord involvement

shortlist.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral, symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions and spinal cord involvement

shortlist.label: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple bilateral, symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions and rapid progression of neurological deficits

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including acute onset of neurological deficits, febrile illness, and respiratory distress, along with the presence of multiple bilateral symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions on brain MRI and diffuse T2 hyperintensities throughout the spinal cord, are consistent with Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM). The lack of albuminocytologic dissociation in the cerebrospinal fluid also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute Transverse Myelitis
rejected.why: While the patient has spinal cord involvement, the presence of brain lesions and the lack of isolated spinal cord symptoms make ADEM a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
rejected.why: The patient's brain lesions are not limited to the areas typically affected in NMOSD, and the absence of optic neuritis makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Multiple Sclerosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with a monophasic illness, and the lack of oligoclonal bands in the cerebrospinal fluid makes MS less likely.

rejected.label: Guillain-Barre Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms, including the presence of brain lesions and the lack of ascending paralysis, are not consistent with GBS.
